Course: "10. Tissues and Its Types" · subject: Science and Technology · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.
[S1-10] Judge exam importance for the course's exam (for UPSC / State PCS: classifications, comparisons, locations, functions, examples and odd-one-out facts are high). Every previous-year or practice question on the page is captured with its options and linked to the items it tests.
[S1-12] Connect the whole chapter: group items into concepts; record how concepts relate (part of, type of, depends on, causes, contrasts with, example of, sequence); resolve every cross-reference such as 'Fig. 6.10' to its item; list only the prerequisites this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite (no chains), each with why it is needed and the chapter concepts that need it; the rule is not a number: usually that is 8 or fewer, more than 8 needs a stated reason why every one is directly needed, and a directly needed prerequisite is never dropped to reach a number; propose a teaching order that starts from what the student already knows.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a trim_prerequisites card:
- card.parts are the chapter map's current prerequisites (part_id = id "pre1", "pre2" ...); card.coverage.must_cover lists them all:
  each id must be in the from_ids of exactly one kept prerequisite or in dropped.
- The source lists the chapter's concepts (id | name | type | core explanation) and the current prerequisites
  (id | name | basis | needed for | why).
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the chapter needs, your main keep, merge and drop decisions with a reason each, what is
  uncertain.
- prerequisites: only what a student must already understand to follow this chapter's concepts directly; never a prerequisite of a
  prerequisite (if A is needed only to understand prerequisite B, drop A or fold it into B in one simple line); merge overlapping ones.
  Usually that is 8 or fewer, but never drop one the chapter directly needs to reach a number. Each: name (short, in clear
  English), why_needed (one sentence), needed_for (the chapter concept ids that need it directly), basis ("book" or "outside"),
  from_ids (the current ids it keeps or merges).
- dropped: every current prerequisite that is not kept or merged, with the reason (only background for another prerequisite; taught
  in the chapter itself; not needed to follow the chapter; ...).
- prerequisite_note: "" when you keep 8 or fewer; with more, why every kept one is directly needed (BIE's code asks for it).
BIE teaches the kept prerequisites in one 5-8 minute "pehle yeh jaan lo" video, so each must be small and concrete.
Reply with the JSON object only.

pre1 | Cell boundary, cytoplasm, nucleus and the cell as a functional unit | outside | c01, c02, c03, c06, c07, c08, c09, c10, c11, c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c17, c18, c19, c20, c21, c22, c24, c25, c26, c27, c28, c29, c30, c31, c32, c33 | Outside basis: Establish what belongs inside one cell, what lies outside it, and why a cell can have a specialised function; revisit nucleus position and number before interpreting epithelial, muscle, blood and plant-cell drawings.

pre10 | Epithelial regeneration, keratin, abrasion and tight junctions | outside | c09, c10, c11 | Outside basis: Explain replacement of shed cells, frictional wear, a keratin-rich protective surface and close cell junctions before interpreting stratified, keratinised and transitional epithelia.

prerequisites.name: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and basic plant-cell parts
prerequisites.why_needed: Cell ke andar aur bahar ka fark, nucleus, wall, vacuole aur chloroplast pehchanne se tissue-cell structure aur living/dead cell comparisons samajh aate hain.

prerequisites.name: Chromosome sets, DNA copying and nuclear versus cell division
prerequisites.why_needed: Diploid/haploid sets, copied chromosomes, nuclear division versus cytoplasmic separation, spindle/centriole/aster ke brief meanings aur somatic versus reproductive cells ka fark mitosis–meiosis tables padhne ke liye chahiye.

prerequisites.name: Body covering, cavity, lumen and gland duct
prerequisites.why_needed: Hollow organ ke andar ke space, uski lining, exposed surface aur underlying tissue ka spatial relation epithelial layers aur gland formation ko samajhne deta hai.

prerequisites.name: Diffusion, absorption and secretion
prerequisites.why_needed: Concentration difference se movement, uptake aur release ka fark epithelial structure ko uske exchange function se jodne ke liye chahiye; cilia aur microvilli chapter ke saath samjhaye jayenge.

prerequisites.name: Strength, flexibility, elasticity and rigidity
prerequisites.why_needed: Pull ko resist karna, bend hona, stretch ke baad shape recover karna aur stiff rehna alag properties hain, jinse animal aur plant supporting tissues ke functions samajh aate hain.

prerequisites.name: Contraction, relaxation, fatigue and voluntary control
prerequisites.why_needed: Force generation, relaxation, performance ghatna aur conscious control ka basic meaning muscle-type comparisons samajhne ke liye chahiye, bina cellular energy pathways padhe.

prerequisites.name: Root and shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth
prerequisites.why_needed: Plant ke in positions aur length versus thickness ka fark jaanna meristem location aur growth-direction comparisons ko meaningful banata hai.

prerequisites.name: Photosynthesis, food storage and root water–mineral uptake
prerequisites.why_needed: Leaves mein food banana, cells mein food store hona aur roots se water–minerals lena samajhne se parenchyma aur transport tissues ke alag kaam clear hote hain.

notes.about: Review of the trimmed prerequisites for Chapter 10 (Tissues and Its Types). The maker trimmed 30 candidate prerequisites down to 8 essential, concrete prerequisite groups while dropping tissue-specific outcomes and in-chapter anatomical examples.
key_questions: Are all 30 original prerequisites accounted for in either prerequisites[].from_ids or dropped[].id?
Were any truly necessary prior concepts dropped, or were any chapter-taught outcomes wrongly kept as prerequisites?
Do the merged prerequisites preserve the essential concepts needed before starting the chapter?

decisions.decision: Pass the trimmed prerequisite set with minor suggestions.
decisions.reason: All 30 items are accounted for, circular prerequisites (things the chapter itself teaches, like extracellular matrix, tendons/ligaments, neuron synapse, differentiation, lignin, xylem/phloem anatomy, cuticle, stomata) were rightly dropped to be taught in-chapter, and the 8 kept prerequisites are genuine foundational concepts.

problems.where: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and basic plant-cell parts (from_ids: pre1, pre2)
problems.problem: needed_for omits a few concepts (such as c16, c17, c26, c27) where uninucleate/living/dead protoplast and cell-wall features are directly compared before the summary tables.
problems.fix: Consider including c16, c17, c26 and c27 in needed_for, or keep as is since c18 and c28 cover the comparisons.

problems.where: Root and shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth (from_ids: pre21)
problems.problem: The term 'bark' from pre21 is omitted from the title and why_needed, even though c23 and c35 explicitly describe lateral meristem as present 'beneath the bark'.
problems.fix: Mention 'bark' in why_needed alongside root/shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth.

checklist.note: All retained prerequisites are properly marked with basis 'outside' and represent standard, accurate foundational biology.
A top UPSC/State PCS teacher would agree with trimming circular tissue-level details out of the prerequisites and keeping only cell, division, spatial, and basic physiological foundations.
The maker's notes clearly state what the unit is about, the main trimming/merging decisions with reasons, and uncertainties.
No teachable book content is lost; items dropped from prerequisites are explicitly delegated to the chapter concepts where the book actually teaches or tests them.
Every prerequisite's basis is accurately marked as 'outside' and the conceptual explanations are standard and correct.

The 8 retained prerequisites are concrete, foundational concepts (basic cell parts, ploidy/division basics, lumen/duct geometry, diffusion/secretion, mechanical properties, muscle contraction/fatigue basics, basic plant organ geometry, and photosynthesis/uptake basics) that a student genuinely needs before studying tissues.
Links to practice and PYQ concepts (c35, c40, c42) in needed_for are sensible and relevant for UPSC/State PCS.
Only direct prerequisites are listed, prerequisite chains and circular chapter outcomes have been removed, and needed_for links connect cleanly to the chapter map.
